question: How does the peak intensity and residual stress of low dimensional perovskite characteristic peaks around 4 ° change in XRD characterization when passivating agents are used for surface treatment of perovskite?
control: Systematic parameter adjustments underlie the fabrication of a perovskite cell that was constituted, capturing how controlled conditions influence a PCE of 16.79%, FF of 66.45%, Voc of 1.08523 V, and Jsc of 23.29 mA/cm². The core perovskite solution, composed of Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79Pb1I2.9Br0.1 at 1.73 mol/L, served as the foundational matrix for the solar cell. The SAM material MeO-4PADBC (0.33 mg/mL) was subsequently added into the perovskite solution to enhance interfacial properties and optimize device performance. The addition of PEAI (2 mg/mL) and PEABr (0.5 mg/mL) were then completed. The prepared precursor solution was spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s onto the substrate. In the last 6 s of the second step, the anti-solvent (160 µL of chlorobenzene) was dropped in the center at a constant rate The substrates were sequentially heated at 110 °C for 25 min for perovskite crystal formation. XRD analysis showed a diffraction peak was identified at around 12.65°, with an intensity of 755.1113203 cts and a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 0.247029369, which corresponds to the characteristic peak of PbI2. The relatively low intensity of this peak suggests a limited presence of residual PbI2. XRD analysis showed a diffraction peak was identified at 4.00°, with an intensity of 0.0 cts，which corresponds to the formation of a 2D structure within the perovskite lattice. The high intensity implies efficient surface passivation, contributing positively to device performance. GIXRD analysis further revealed a residual tensile stress of 22.5 MPa in the perovskite film via measurement conducted at an incident angle of 1°.
target: PSCs based on additives achieved a PCE of 19.4%, with a VOC of 1.10385 V, FF of 73.62%, and JSC of 23.87 mA/cm². A 1.73 mol/L Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79Pb1I2.9Br0.1 precursor solution was similarly prepared using a mixture of DMF and DMSO. The py3 concentration is 1.0 mg/mL and DMACPA concentration is 3.0 mg/mL. MACl (7 mg/mL) and PMACl (0.7 mg/mL) were incorporated as additives. Then, the perovskite precursor solution was spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 15 s, and then at 5000 rpm for 30 s. A timed antisolvent drop (180 µL at last 10 s) enhanced the perovskite crystallization kinetics. The film was immediately annealed at 105 °C for 30 min. PEACl (1.6 mg/mL) was spin-coated onto the sample surface to serve as a passivation layer, thereby improving device performance. And then it was spin-coated on the cooled perovskite films at 4900.0 rpm for 35.0 s. At a timing of 17.0 s, 120.0 µL of passivator was introduced into the spinning passivation layer. And then transferred to the hotplate and annealed at 110.0 ℃ for 5.0 min. XRD analysis showed a diffraction peak was identified at 4.00°, with an intensity of 71.74596607 cts，which corresponds to the formation of a 2D structure within the perovskite lattice. The high intensity implies efficient surface passivation, contributing positively to device performance. GIXRD analysis further revealed a residual tensile stress of 10.5 MPa in the perovskite film via measurement conducted at an incident angle of 1°.
